item.title: Real Madrid rejected the chance to sign Barcelona attacking star back in the summer – Romano
item.description: Real Madrid rejected the chance to sign Barcelona attacking star back in the summer – Romano Real Madrid had a very busy summer transfer window, bringing in a number of reinforcements to support Jose Mourinho’s new project at the club. Los Blancos made many smart free-agent signings but also broke the bank to sign Yan Diomande from RB Leipzig. Ahead of the season’s first El Clasico , it has now emerged that Madrid turned down an opportunity to sign Karim Adeyemi, instead pursuing a move for the Ivory Coast winger. Adeyemi went on to sign for Barcelona, where he has made a good start to life at his new club. According to Fabrizio Romano (h/t Madrid Zone ), Borussia Dortmund offered the Germany international to Los Blancos as a potential market opportunity. However, Madrid did not make a move. Real Madrid opted against signing Adeyemi Adeyemi was approaching the final year of his Dortmund contract and had no intention of signing an extension. The Bundesliga club were exploring multiple destinations, including Madrid, Barcelona and some Premier League clubs. Real Madrid chose Yan Diomande over Karim Adeyemi back in the summer. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) However, Madrid’s recruitment strategy was focused on a different attacking profile, leading them to reject the opportunity. Adeyemi eventually joined Barcelona, a club he had wanted to represent since childhood. Interestingly, Barcelona had also considered Diomande earlier this summer. The Catalan club eventually signed Anthony Gordon from Newcastle United before signing Adeyemi. Why Madrid preferred Diomande Madrid ultimately committed €125 million plus €15 million in potential bonuses to secure Diomande, underlining their belief in his long-term potential. The 19-year-old has already begun demonstrating why the club invested so heavily, particularly through his recent attacking contributions. His explosive dribbling, acceleration and ability to beat defenders individually offer Mourinho a direct threat from wide areas. Diomande is in line to start El Clasico later today , with Vinicius Junior currently serving a suspension. Diomande is expected to start against Barcelona at the Camp Nou. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) Adeyemi would have represented a considerably cheaper alternative, but the two players bring different qualities. The German’s pace and versatility could have strengthened Madrid’s attacking depth. However, he does not have the same kind of ceiling as Diomande. Ultimately, with both players securing the moves they wanted, this is nothing more than summer transfer window trivia. It remains to be seen whether Adeyemi and Diomande come face-to-face in tonight’s Clasico and who goes on to have the bigger influence on the game.

item.title: Jack Miller says Australian GP cancellation “tough to swallow”: “It is pissing me off”
item.description: Motorsport photo Jack Miller has conceded he feels “pissed off” by the cancellation of the Australian Grand Prix, saying missing out on one final MotoGP race in front of his home crowd was “tough to swallow”. Low visibility rendered the medical helicopter inoperable at Phillip Island, forcing race control to scrap all track action scheduled for Sunday, including the main premier class event. The decision brought a disappointing end to Phillip Island’s tenure as a MotoGP venue, with the popular 4.4km circuit set to be replaced by a new urban track in Adelaide next year. But the news also came as a major blow to Pramac rider Miller, who was hoping to make one final appearance at his home circuit as a MotoGP rider before switching to the World Superbike Championship next year. The Australian thanked fans who had braved the weather to attend the event, expressing his disappointment that they had been denied the chance to watch their favourite riders race. “It's a little different to how things began for WG [Wayne Gardner] back in '89,” he said, referring to the first MotoGP race at Phillip Island nearly four decades ago. “You fans have been amazing throughout all the years,” he said on the grid ahead of the parade laps. “My little decade here, you guys have been the best. “I can only speak on behalf of the other boys. item.description: 🎥 He's already on a yellow! Linesman sends player tumbling It's the refereeing team's job to make sure a match is as fair as possible and the players stay on their feet. item.title: Bayern Munich reportedly "decided against" signing Manzambi last summer
item.description: Bayern Munich reportedly "decided against" signing Manzambi last summer Bayern Munich could apparently have signed Johan Manzambi last summer before Aston Villa met SC Freiburg's asking price. According to Sky Germany, the Munich club seriously considered the Swiss international but ultimately opted to drop their transfer plans. "Well, he's a player they were interested in last summer. They could have signed him then. But nothing came of it. "They decided against the signing," explained the pay-TV channel's chief reporter Florian Plettenberg regarding Bayern's intentions. The decision at the time was apparently based on the conviction that Bayern held sufficient quality in their own squad in central midfield. As a result, the Bavarian giants relied on their existing options and therefore refrained from making a serious move for Manzambi. The 21-year-old instead moved from Freiburg to Aston Villa, with the Premier League club paying €70million in the Swiss international. In his first six competitive matches for Villa, Manzambi has already made a name for himself by contributing six goals and assists. With good form changing his economic valuation, Plettenberg senses a move to Bayern down the line now seems highly unlikely “It's simply no longer financially feasible for Bayern. It's a transfer, and it's just incredibly unrealistic at the moment," he concluded.

item.title: 'He's a machine!' - Arsenal legend Martin Keown hails 'legendary' Gabriel and names Premier League's best defensive duo
item.description: Arsenal FC v Everton - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Arsenal icon Martin Keown has heaped praise on Gabriel Magalhaes following the Gunners' commanding Premier League victory over Everton. The Brazilian defender was labelled a "legend of the football club" as Mikel Arteta's side moved level on points with Manchester City at the top of the table. Arsenal secure vital victory over Everton Arsenal took full advantage of a City slip-up by securing a comfortable 2-0 victory over Everton at the Emirates Stadium. Summer signing Ezri Konsa opened the scoring after just seven minutes, poking the ball home to give the hosts a perfect start. Brazilian centre-back Gabriel then put the game to bed with a decisive 68th-minute header. The result marked Arsenal's third consecutive Premier League win and saw Arteta's side join City at the top of the table on 21 points. Keown labels Gabriel a club legend Following the commanding defensive display, former Arsenal stalwart Keown reserved special praise for Gabriel. Speaking on BBC's Match of the Day , the former player was quick to highlight the Brazilian's immense contribution to the club. "Gabriel is into his sixth season at Arsenal now and this guy is just a machine," Keown stated. "You rarely see a striker get the better of him. I’ve seen him mature a lot and become the leader at the back. He was immense again today. He just loves defending and the fans just buzz of him. He’s a legend of the football club now." Konsa hailed as an outstanding signing Keown also turned his attention to Konsa, who joined Arsenal in a £55 million deal from Aston Villa . The pundit noted how seamlessly the England international has slotted into a defensive unit that already features William Saliba. "I’ve got so much admiration for him and how he’s come into the club, he’s been a great signing," Keown explained. "They already had a number of great central defenders but him coming into the team has been seamless. He’s been magnificent, it’s a really outstanding signing for Arsenal." Praising the new centre-back pairing, Keown added: "You look at that partnership with Gabriel, I don’t see a better one in the Premier League right now. He’s come in and not been overshadowed at all." Arsenal look to build on momentum The victory over Everton proved especially significant after title rivals City suffered a defeat against Aston Villa earlier in the day. Arteta's men will now briefly turn their attention away from Premier League action. The Gunners return to the pitch on Tuesday night when they face League Two strugglers Fleetwood Town in the fourth round of the EFL Cup.

item.title: What Connor McCaffery’s brother had to say about Caitlin Clark’s All-WNBA First Team selection
item.description: Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images Caitlin Clark has earned her place on the All-WNBA First Team for the second time in her career, prompting a proud reaction from Patrick McCaffery, the younger brother of her boyfriend, Connor McCaffery. Patrick celebrated the Indiana Fever star’s achievement on social media while also sending a message to those who have criticised her. Clark first earned First Team honours during her rookie season in 2024, but injuries restricted her to just 13 appearances the following year. She returned to full strength this season and quickly reminded the league of her influence. Patrick McCaffery sends message to Caitlin Clark’s critics after All-WNBA selection Patrick took to Instagram to celebrate Clark’s latest recognition, writing: “yeahhhh did it again yall stay mad”. His reaction came after the WNBA announced its five All-WNBA First Team selections: Clark, Kelsey Mitchell, A’ja Wilson, Breanna Stewart and Olivia Miles. Nike also joined the celebrations, commenting on a post shared by the Fever: “This vote wasn’t complicated”. The Indiana Pacers echoed that sentiment with a simple message: “Never a doubt”. Clark’s numbers help explain the excitement surrounding her selection. She averaged 22.3 points and 8.3 assists per game during the regular season, ranking third in scoring and second in assists. She also recorded more 25-point, 10-assist games this season than any other player has managed across their career. The recognition was particularly significant for Indiana, with Mitchell joining Clark on the First Team after a record-breaking campaign of her own. Mitchell scored 1,086 points during the regular season, setting a new WNBA single-season record, while her average of 24.7 points per game established a new Fever franchise record. However, the individual honours come after Indiana’s playoff campaign ended in the first round against Wilson’s Las Vegas Aces. The Fever now face important decisions ahead of next season, with Mitchell entering free agency and the franchise needing to strengthen its roster around Clark and Aliyah Boston. Keeping that core together will be a major priority as Indiana looks to turn its star power into a championship challenge. item.title: Liverpool Starting XI vs Brighton: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup
item.description: Liverpool Starting XI vs Brighton: Confirmed Team News and Predicted Lineup Liverpool Team News vs Brighton: Bradley Barcola Fit as Andoni Iraola Weighs Key Calls Liverpool have one immediate concern off the table ahead of Brighton’s visit to Anfield. Bradley Barcola is available. The winger missed the open section of training earlier in the week, which prompted the usual noise around fitness, but there is no issue now. Andoni Iraola made that clear in his pre-match briefing, saying: “Bradley has trained today normally, he is fine. It was no problem, just a matter of sometimes you have have to deal with the load and consider sometimes they have to stay inside but he is fine.” That matters because Barcola has been a constant presence in Liverpool’s Premier League side since arriving from Paris Saint-Germain in a £123 million summer move. If Iraola starts him against Brighton, that run continues. Barcola fitness boosts Liverpool options Barcola’s availability gives Iraola a real decision in the wide areas. Rio Ngumoha and Cody Gakpo both caught the eye in midweek, and Florian Wirtz also pushed his case with a goal from the bench. Those are useful problems to have, though they still need solving properly. One change looks simple enough. Alexander Isak should come back into the side in place of Lewis Koumas. Beyond that, the more interesting call is behind him. If Wirtz returns to the starting line-up, Ryan Gravenberch would be against Trey Nyoni for a start alongside Alexis Mac Allister. Photo: IMAGO Injury update before Brighton clash Not everyone is ready. Dominik Szoboszlai remains out with a hamstring problem. He is training individually, which is progress, but not enough for Sunday. Jeremie Frimpong is expected to miss around a month with a muscle injury. Hugo Ekitike, Giovanni Leoni and Conor Bradley also remain sidelined. Victor Munoz is the one uncertainty. The winger picked up a minor knee issue in the comeback win over Brentford and missed the midweek match. His status remains unclear. Likely Liverpool XI at Anfield This is Liverpool’s second of four straight home games across three competitions, so squad management matters. Villarreal have already been beaten in the Champions League, Chelsea are next in the Carabao Cup, and Arsenal follow in the league. Brighton arrive in the middle of that run, and Iraola has enough depth to rotate without weakening the side too much. The likeliest shape is a 4-2-3-1: Alisson, Araujo, Jacquet, Van Dijk, Kerkez, Mac Allister, Nyoni, Ngumoha, Wirtz, Barcola, Isak. Kick-off at Anfield is 2pm GMT on Sunday, October 25.

item.title: Barcelona superstar discusses Vinicius Jr., Fede Valverde and Jose Mourinho ahead of Real Madrid clash
item.description: Barcelona superstar discusses Vinicius Jr., Fede Valverde and Jose Mourinho ahead of Real Madrid clash Real Madrid are preparing for arguably the biggest game of the season, and Jose Mourinho’s team will want the three points on their trip to the Spotify Camp Nou . Ahead of the game, Barcelona captain Raphinha has shared his thoughts on Real Madrid’s preparations for El Clasico . The Brazilian has spoken about his compatriot Vinicius Junior’s suspension, Fede Valverde’s versatility and Jose Mourinho’s return to the Camp Nou . Raphinha refuses to underestimate Madrid without Vinicius The Brazilian winger was asked whether Vinicius’ absence would benefit Barcelona, and Raphinha refused to underestimate Los Blancos . “I can’t say his absence will be good for us, because Real Madrid ultimately have many players capable of deciding matches,” Raphinha explained (h/t FCB World ). “It’s true that Vini won’t be there, but there are other players who can play in his position and make the difference in a match of this magnitude.” Raphinha refuses to underestimate Real Madrid despite the absence of Vinicius Jr. (Photo by Edilzon Gamez/Getty Images) His words reflect the quality and depth Madrid have in their attack and the threat they can pose to their opponents. Mourinho can turn to alternative attacking options, including Yan Diomande, while Kylian Mbappe remains a major threat through the middle. For Madrid, the challenge is finding the right attacking balance rather than simply replacing Vinicius’ individual qualities. Valverde earns praise as Mourinho prepares for Camp Nou return Raphinha was particularly complimentary about Valverde, who could feature at right-back rather than in his usual midfield role. “Fede can make runs from midfield and give the team plenty of options when he plays at full-back,” the Brazilian said . “He’s an incredible player who performs brilliantly in midfield and also does an excellent job out wide.” Raphinha also named the Uruguayan and Jude Bellingham as the engines that keep Madrid functioning. Raphinha is full of praise for his counterpart, Fede Valverde. (Photo by Yasser Bakhsh/Getty Images) Asked about Mourinho’s return to the Camp Nou , Raphinha admitted he could not predict the reception the former Madrid manager would receive. “When Mourinho was here before, I wasn’t around, so I can’t tell you what to expect from the fans,” he explained . “What I want is for our supporters to be behind us from beginning to end, whatever happens during the match.” Those last quotes from Raphinha highlight the challenge that lies ahead for Jose Mourinho’s team later today. Barcelona will have home support and a six-point league advantage, even if Raphinha recognises Madrid’s strengths. Los Blancos need to play a near-perfect game to get the three points against Barça , and it remains to be seen how the game plays out.

item.title: Bundesliga coaches reflect on relentless demands of the job after Vincent Kompany collapse
item.description: Bundesliga coaches reflect on relentless demands of the job after Vincent Kompany collapse Vincent Kompany’s collapse on Friday has prompted a number of coaches across German football to reflect on the demands of their profession while sending their best wishes to the Bayern Munich head coach. Kompany collapsed while watching Bayern’s reserve team train at the Säbener Straße on Friday and was subsequently taken to hospital. Having struggled with a viral infection since the previous weekend, Kompany was initially considered doubtful for Bayern’s Champions League fixture against Arsenal on Wednesday . The Bayern coach nevertheless returned to the touchline and handled the club’s post-match media duties. Bayern have confirmed that the 40-year-old is in a stable condition and will remain under medical supervision while further examinations are carried out. Board Member for Sport Max Eberl has indicated that Kompany’s absence is likely to be measured in weeks rather than days. Several of Kompany’s coaching colleagues addressed the situation before or after their Bundesliga and 2. Bundesliga fixtures this weekend. Kicker and the Deutsche Presse-Agentur collected a number of their reactions. Miroslav Klose (1. FC Nürnberg) “I was shocked too. It’s not easy to look after yourself as a coach, because we’re all stubborn. We have to carve out free time for ourselves to clear our heads. I notice it myself: I have one day a week where I really try to leave a little earlier. But I don’t always manage it.” Miron Muslic (Schalke 04) “I know it. The day is sometimes very, very long. Our job is very demanding. That’s why — as we say in Austria — ‘coaching hygiene’ is very important. I wish Vincent all the very best. I hope it’s nothing too serious and that we see him back on the touchline soon.” Niko Kovac (Borussia Dortmund) “The important thing in this phase is to give him peace and quiet. He needs the time. We all know how exhausting a coaching job like this is.” Daniel Thioune (Werder Bremen) “I used a moment in the dressing room before the game to send him a message. After the final whistle, I saw that he had already replied. That shows that he’s probably already doing a little better. “From my side, only the very best wishes. We’re opponents so often, but as coaching colleagues we also stick together and know that health is our most valuable asset.” Thioune’s comments underlined the sense of solidarity among coaches despite the competitive nature of their work. Martin Demichelis (RB Leipzig) “As coaches, we think 24 hours a day about what we can improve. Our heads probably work far too much. He’s a tough guy as well and has an incredible personality and a lot of passion. I wish him rest and a speedy recovery.” Urs Fischer (1. FSV Mainz 05) “Of course you notice something like that. It’s not nice, but it’s part of life. At this point, I wish Vincent a speedy recovery and send my best wishes to Munich. I hope he comes back as quickly as possible.” GGFN | Peter

item.title: 'If you don't believe, you've already failed!' – Hero Maxi Beier speaks out after Dortmund thunderbolt
item.description: Borussia Dortmund v Eintracht Frankfurt - Bundesliga 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Borussia Dortmund forward Maxi Beier expressed delight after coming off the bench to score the decisive goal in BVB's 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt. The German attacker highlighted the importance of belief and relentless training routines. Beier strike seals dramatic three points for Black and Yellows Maxi Beier produced a moment of magic in the 80th minute to hand Borussia Dortmund a 1-0 victory over Eintracht Frankfurt at a sold-out Signal Iduna Park. Beier initiated the move on the left wing, feeding substitute Jobe Bellingham before receiving a precise lay-off. The 68th-minute substitute unleashed a curling 17-metre effort past Frankfurt goalkeeper Noah Atubolu into the far top corner. The goal secured BVB's fifth win of the Bundesliga campaign, taking them to the top of the table. Forward credits relentless practice for far-corner specialty Speaking to Sky after the final whistle, Beier revealed that his spectacular long-range finish was no accident. "I practice those shots a lot in training," Beier explained. "Of course, I’m happy that it went in like that. Believing in [our ability to score late] is the most important thing." "If you don’t believe in it, you've already failed," the forward asserted. Beier embraces demanding schedule amid BVB winning run Despite BVB navigating a brutal run of matches across European and domestic competitions, Beier insisted the squad thrives under heavy workloads. "It’s been a demanding few weeks so far," Beier admitted. "But we all love the game and being out on the field." Beier's decisive contribution validated Niko Kovac's second-half tactical substitutions. Dortmund attacker aims to maintain goalscoring touch Beier's goal-scoring form provides Kovac with potent offensive options ahead of a crucial stretch in Dortmund's season. BVB turn their attention to a midweek DFB-Pokal tie against Werder Bremen before facing Bayern Munich. The German international will look to keep his spot in Kovac's attacking rotation.

item.title: Matt Barnes gives Angel Reese her flowers despite always being ‘pinned up’ against Caitlin Clark
item.description: Photo by Colin Hubbard/Getty Images Matt Barnes wants Angel Reese to get some more credit despite consistently being compared with Caitlin Clark. Reese has had a stellar season since being traded to the Atlanta Dream and is just two wins away from winning her first WNBA championship. But for the last few years, since before she entered the league, Reese has consistently been compared to her rival, Caitlin Clark, ever since they faced off in the NCAA National Championship tournament. Matt Barnes praises Angel Reese for ‘looking pretty’ in debate against Caitlin Clark Speaking on Kevin Garnett’s podcast, former NBA star Matt Barnes praised Angel Reese for the way she has performed all season, especially in the WNBA Finals. He applauded Reese for handling the pressure of the public pitting her against Caitlin Clark very well, and suggested that she has taken her game to another level. Barnes said: “She’s trending towards Finals MVP if they win it. I feel Angel Reese has got a lot of s*** to get to this point. I think she’s always been pinned up against Caitlin Clark. “It’s the white Barbie superhero versus the black hood ‘girl.’ She’s out here putting nasty double-doubles. Talking s***, knocking down threes. Looking pretty out there.” So far in the WNBA Finals, Reese has averaged 18.3 points, 12.3 rebounds, 2.3 assists, 1.8 steals, and 1.5 blocks per game while shooting 47.1% from the field and a staggering 60.0% from beyond the arc. Perhaps what stands out most to fans is Reese’s efficiency from deep, especially considering how much of a weakness it had been for her. Should she help lead the Dream to the WNBA Championship, Reese will have a significant edge over Clark in their rivalry. Not only did Reese help lead LSU to victory against Clark and Iowa en route to the NCAA Championship, but a win for the Dream means she would also boast a WNBA Championship trophy over Clark, who is yet to win a playoff series. item.title: Liverpool given warning that Andoni Iraola simply can't ignore
item.description: Liverpool given warning that Andoni Iraola simply can't ignore Andoni Iraola has only lost one game as Liverpool's head coach so far. And, while that may seem like a solid record, the way that Liverpool have managed to win games has been rather lucky. They've barely scored any goals but, because their defence has been fairly solid, they've managed to scrape the odd three points here and there. At the moment, they're not in contention for the title but, if they can iron out the problems that they're facing and potentially add some new talent to their ranks in January, they could be well on their way to the top of the Premier League table. Jeremie Frimpong's new injury highlights Liverpool's need for a new right-back Last term, Liverpool's right-back was a major problem for them. So much so, that both Curtis Jones and Dominik Szoboszlai had to do extended stints as full-backs . And, while the midfielders performances were surprisingly impressive, they weren't full-time solutions. So, that's what led to Ronald Araujo being brought in. The Uruguayan had done a stellar job during his time at Anfield but, with all the injuries that have been occurring, it's now clear that a new right-back should be one of Liverpool's main priorities. Several different players have been mentioned as potential options and, even though Conor Bradley could return and get straight back to his best , it's unclear how he's going to perform after his return from injury. And, while Frimpong was brought in last summer to try and help fill the void left by Trent Alexander-Arnold , his injuries are clearly impacting his ability to make a difference, which, for a team who want to be competing for silverware every season, is far from ideal. So, that's why, in January, a new right-back may have just moved to the top of Liverpool's priority list. item.title: “We win and lose together”: Alonso shows faith in Penders after Chelsea’s Spurs setback
item.description: “We win and lose together”: Alonso shows faith in Penders after Chelsea’s Spurs setback Xabi Alonso has said Chelsea have full confidence in Mike Penders despite the goalkeeper's mistake in defeat to Tottenham. Penders was at fault for Tottenham's opening goal during the 2-0 defeat at Stamford Bridge, as the 21-year-old punched Mateus Fernandes' set piece into his goal. The error compounded a miserable night for Chelsea, who lost at home to Spurs in the Premier League for only the second time in 36 years. Alonso's side also had Cole Palmer sent off for two needless bookings, before Mathys Tel fired home a late second to seal the win. Penders was making his first Premier League start for the West Londoners, after Emi Martinez underwent surgery on a broken jaw sustained against Everton. Alonso admitted that mistakes are a part of football and underlined his confidence in Penders. He said the young goalkeeper would remain in goal for Wednesday night's Carabao Cup tie at Liverpool. "It’s part of the business; you need to deal with mistakes and we keep confidence in Mike and he will be in goal against Liverpool," Alonso said at full-time. "We win and we lose together and it’s part of the job to deal with mistakes, myself as well as everyone. "We support Mike and Geo (Quenda) as well, the guys starting their first [Premier League] games. He will want to prove he can do better - and we also have to show that."

item.title: Ballon d’Or ceremony returns to England in nod to ‘revolutionary’ Stanley Matthews
item.description: Matthews’ family ‘very excited’ as London Palladium hosts event 70 years after first award at Blackpool town hall When football’s dignitaries assemble on Monday at the London Palladium for the Ballon d’Or ceremony it will be a far cry from the first awards 70 years ago. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. But obviously it’s grown over the years, and now it’s a huge event. We’re very excited.” Continue reading...

item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
